summary: Feed s169_triple to NDR is degraded: 34.1% of TCP sessions are one-way, 17.9% packets are duplicates, and 10.2% frames are sliced to 192 bytes. NDR requires both directions and full payload for reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of each flow to the same NDR tool port. Likely asymmetric routing or flow-unaware load-balancing / separate TAP/SPAN feeds sent to different outputs, so only client->server or server->client arrives.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, session tracking and anomaly detection. With 57/167 sessions (34.1%) one-way, state tracking fails, detections are missed and false positives increase.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR port using symmetric hashing so the NDR sees complete bidirectional sessions for reassembly.

findings.root_cause: Same packets arriving via multiple SPAN/mirror paths or overlapping TAP aggregations without deduplication in the packet broker. 478/2667 packets (17.9%) exceed 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates waste NDR 10G port bandwidth and processing, inflate flow/packet counters, skew analytics, and can trigger duplicate alerts while masking true rates.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short window before forwarding to the NDR, eliminating 17.9% duplicate load.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snap-length enabled and cutting frames to ~192 bytes to save bandwidth. 272/2667 frames (10.2%) are truncated.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection, signature matching and payload anomaly detection. Slicing at 192 bytes removes L7 payload, blinding detection for exploits and C2.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing for this NDR feed so full packets up to the tool's 9216 byte max are forwarded, restoring payload visibility.
